definition: Heroin is an opium-derived narcotic pain-relieving drug that can lead to habit formation. In psychology and learning contexts, it may be discussed as a controlled substance associated with substance use and dependence-related behavior.

provenance.scope: Source record D003932; pinned source text

reasons: The second sentence adds unsupported context (“In psychology and learning contexts”) that is not stated in the packet.
The second sentence also adds unsupported content about “substance use and dependence-related behavior”; the packet only says heroin is a controlled substance and may be habit-forming.

The packet describes heroin as a “narcotic analgesic” that “may be habit-forming” and an “opium derivative” controlled substance; the definition’s framing as “pain-relieving” is only indirectly supported by “analgesic,” and the definition adds claims not present in the packet.

The packet does not state or support that, specifically in “psychology and learning contexts,” heroin is discussed as a controlled substance tied to “substance use and dependence-related behavior.” That psychology/learning-specific claim is not present in the supplied text.
